chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Jahm ibn Abi Jahma, from Mu'tab, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me, while prices had increased in Medina: 'How much food do we have?' I said, 'We have enough for many months.' He said, 'Take it out and sell it.'
He said, 'I said to him, 'But there is no food in Medina.' He said, 'Sell it.' So when I had sold it, he said, 'Buy (food) along with the people day after day.'

And he said, 'O Mu'tab! Make the daily provision for my dependents half barley and half wheat, for Allah knows that I am able to feed them wheat of its own kind, but I love that Allah should see me that I have managed the livelihood in a good way.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on selling goods during inflation and managing household provisions?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Imams' active role in market regulation and alleviating scarcity, as Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) strategically sold stored grain during a price surge to stabilize the Medina market. He emphasized that while he possessed the means to retain premium wheat, he chose to consume barley to demonstrate prudent stewardship (ihsan) and gratitude, thereby modeling ethical economic behavior for his community.
